candidates.term: The Sage inside the Hour Gate
candidates.defline: The Sage lives inside your Hour Gate: underneath your later years is a quiet store of care, given back.
candidates.reading: Accepting help feels strange to you, because for most of your life you have done the looking after. In later life help reaches you anyway, as care from children or younger relatives or someone you trained, and you learn to take it slowly. Your days settle into steady routines of reading, rest and good company, and your mind stays clear on them. You feel smallest in the weeks when nobody needs anything from you, and you rarely say so.
candidates.teaser: The root of your late years is quiet backing: pensions of goodwill, children who shelter you, sleep that comes easily. Kindness banked early pays your old age.

domain_readings.Family: Quiet backing is your late family’s shape: children who shelter you, goodwill banked across decades paying out as care. You taught them how by example. Accept the tending when it comes. They learned it watching you, and refusing it ungrades the lesson.
domain_readings.Health: Kindness banked early pays your old age: sleep that comes easily, a body tended by people who want to tend it. Your late health is communal property in the best sense. Keep the gentle routines and the gentle company. Both are prescription.
domain_readings.Mind: The mind stays clear the way tended gardens stay green: routine, reading, company gentle by default. Late clarity is a maintained garden, never an accident. Keep the daily reading and the weekly conversations. They are the fence and the watering.

candidates.life_chapter: Your late chapter is quietly banked: decades of kindness paying out as shelter, sleep, and company that arrives unbidden. Expect the gentlest old age your line has seen. You built it deposit by deposit. Draw it down without guilt.
candidates.relations: The tending circle is this seat’s people: children, old students, neighbors whose kindness you seeded years back. They arrive with soup and stay for stories. Let them. The circle you fed is feeding back, exactly as designed.
candidates.turn_catalyst: Run thin, the bank goes undrawn: care accrued, withdrawals refused. Accept the next three offers of help outright. It is your money.
candidates.turn_friction: Run heavy, the gentleness settles too deep: tended into passivity. Keep one responsibility that is genuinely yours.
candidates.shadow_line: Overloaded, the sheltered elder stops weathering: protected from life itself.
candidates.health_line: Your late body runs on gentleness and rhythm: soft exercise, regular company, unhurried meals. Managed so, it outlives every prediction.

Family.headline: Your family looks after you, and you let it.
Family.recognition: You are cared for by younger people more than you expected, with visits and help and small kindnesses. Because you are used to being the one who gives, you wave off help you need, and it hurts the people offering. What you want from your family now is company more than help.
Family.lived: Little acts of care have come to you unasked since your late forties, a lift or a meal or a call from younger people. You have found them harder to accept than to give, and you have learned to say yes more often.
Family.ahead: From your late forties the people after you return the care you once gave them, in visits and help you did not ask for. You become the calm centre of a close family in these years, and you take their help without keeping score.

Health.headline: Your health in later life rests on gentle rhythm.
Health.recognition: You stay well on regular meals, unhurried walks and early nights, and you sleep badly the week the rhythm breaks. Because ease restores you, you let the ease run on past the point it helps you, until days with no effort leave you flat and low on energy. You feel best in a week that holds a small challenge.
Health.lived: Your sleep has come more easily since your late forties, and your days have found a steadier pace. You have also gone through a stretch of too much rest, and your energy came back once something asked more of you.
Health.ahead: Your body does well from your late forties on gentle habits and the company of people who look after you. You hold your strength in these years through one demanding thing each week, and you feel the difference whenever you let it go.

Mind.headline: Your mind stays clear through daily habit.
Mind.recognition: You keep your thinking clear with reading, routine and conversation with people who are kind to you. Because your thinking needs calm to work, you avoid arguments and noise, and a year with nothing to puzzle over leaves you restless. You think best with one good question in front of you.
Mind.lived: Daily reading and talks with people you trust have kept your thinking calm and steady since your late forties. You have become the one others ask for a clear view, and you have enjoyed being asked.
Mind.ahead: Reading fills more of your days from your late forties, and you remember more of it than you did in your busiest years. Younger people come to rely on your judgement in these years, and you give it carefully.
